Then slowly rotate the last wheel while pulling the shackle; if you feel or hear a little “click,” the wheel is on a possible number.

1.
Pull the shackle until the last wheel is just short of turning.

You don’t need to cut through metal; you just need to let the wheel protrude 1–2 mm.

3.
Insert the blade tip under that wheel and **twist it forward**.
The internal cam will rotate until the locking lever drops, the shackle releases and the combination is now permanently open.

Afterwards the wheel stays free and you can even push it back into the hole; the lock remains open but you’ll never get another digit sequence out of it.

•
Tap the shackle sideways with a screwdriver and hammer—sometimes the thin spring inside will shift and the lock will pop.
•

None of this is guaranteed, but your lock is really just Sheet metal.
